newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Germany in EMU even if fails some tests - Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Germany in EMU even if fails some tests - Portugal.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said on Tuesday that Germany could join the single currency even if it failed to pass all the economic tests for entry.
He told journalists that providing the reason for Germany's failure was temporary factors and not structural problems, it could still join in 1999.
"I admit the hypothesis (of Germany's entry without strictly satisfying all the criteria)...providing it is for special circumstances and not structural," he said.
Guterres said that a single currency without Germany would make little sense as the "(German) mark has a fundamental role in the future single European currency," he said.

There has been much talk in financial markets that the launch of monetary union could be delayed beyond January 1999 partly because of Germany's perceived problems in meeting the budget deficit target.
"I believe that...Germany is going to make an enormous effort this year to meet the criteria," Guterres said.
